transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really do appreciate it. Um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but it's... it's a little embarrassing to talk about, actually. I don't want you to think badly of me, but I've been experiencing something a bit unusual. 

I've been... well, hearing things. Voices, to be exact. Very clear ones. Mostly when I'm just sitting in my apartment, or sometimes if I'm walking through the empty rooms at the museum. It sounds exactly like women whispering from just behind the walls, and they... they keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I know how strange that must sound, and I’m so sorry if it’s a silly thing to bring up. I try not to let it bother me too much, but... well, am I explaining that okay? Does that make sense to you?
Do the voices ever tell you to do something, or are they just providing information about the photographs?

Oh, um... no, they don't order me around or anything scary like that. I promise it's nothing dangerous. I know that's probably what doctors have to worry about, and I really wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, a risk or anything bad. 

It really is just... just like I mentioned, mostly when I'm in my apartment, or if I'm walking through those empty museum rooms. It's just these very clear voices of women, whispering from behind the walls, and they're just telling me which photographs belong in the archive. They just give me that information, they don't force me to do anything at all. I just try to politely ignore them most of the time so I don't cause a fuss. 

Is that... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm being helpful. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Do you feel like the voices are coming from inside your head or from outside, like they're really coming from behind the walls?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound completely crazy, Doctor. I know how important it is to be honest with you, though. 

It definitely feels like they're coming from outside. Like I said, it's... it's just like women whispering from right behind the walls. It doesn't feel like it's just my own thoughts or anything inside my head. It's very distinct, very clear. Mostly in my apartment, or, you know, those empty rooms at the museum. They just keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I know it sounds so strange to say out loud, and I'm really sorry if it's a bother to listen to. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Are the voices something you hear all the time when you're in those places, or do they come and go?

Oh, um... they definitely come and go. It's not constant, thank goodness. I wouldn't want to be a bother to anyone if it was happening all the time. 

It's really just... well, like I mentioned before, it's mostly when it's very quiet. Just in my apartment, or sometimes if I'm walking through the empty rooms at the museum. That's when I hear them—those clear voices, like women whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. 

But it's not every single time I'm there, and I really do try my best to just go about my day normally when it happens. I hope that's the right way to handle it. Am I... am I giving you too much of the same information? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question properly, Doctor.
Do the voices happen when you're feeling stressed or anxious, or can they occur when you're feeling calm?

Oh, um... they can happen when I'm calm, actually. I hope that doesn't mean I'm doing something wrong to bring them on. 

I'll just be sitting quietly in my apartment, reading or having a cup of tea, completely relaxed, and then... there they are. Those clear voices of women whispering from behind the walls, just letting me know which photographs belong in the archive. Or sometimes when I'm at the museum, just peacefully walking through those empty rooms, not feeling stressed at all. 

I really try to keep my stress levels down, Doctor, because I know that's important for my health. I wouldn't want you to think I'm not managing my anxiety well. I hope it's okay that they happen even when I'm calm... does that make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it in a way that helps you.
Have you ever seen, smelled, tasted, or felt anything that wasn't really there, besides hearing the voices?

Oh, um... no, no, nothing like that. I really hope that's the right answer. 

I haven't... I haven't seen anything that isn't there, or smelled anything strange. I try very hard to keep a clean home, so I'd definitely notice if there was an odd smell, and I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm imagining things like that. It's really just... just the whispering I mentioned before. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything else to report about that. I wouldn't want to waste your time by making things up, you know? I just want to be as helpful and accurate as possible. Am I doing okay with these questions, Doctor?
Can you make the voices stop when you want them to?

Oh, um... I wish I could. I really do try my best to just... will them away, because I know I shouldn't be hearing them. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting there letting it happen without trying to be proactive about it. 

But... no, I can't really make them stop. Like I was saying before about those clear voices—the women whispering from behind the walls about which photographs belong in the archive—when they start up in my apartment or when I'm in those empty museum rooms, I just kind of have to wait for them to finish. I try very hard to just ignore them and be good, but they have a mind of their own, it seems. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or... or like I'm not trying hard enough to get better. I really am trying, Doctor. Is it... is it okay that I can't stop them on my own? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to be doing.
Do the voices ever say anything negative or critical about you?

Oh, no... no, they don't say anything mean. I hope that's a good thing? I wouldn't want to be the sort of person who has... well, bad things said about them. 

Like I mentioned, it's really just those clear voices... the women whispering from behind the walls in my apartment, or sometimes when I'm walking through those empty museum rooms. They just talk about the photographs, you know? Telling me which ones belong in the archive. They're actually quite polite about it. 

I really hope that's what you were looking for. I know some people hear very scary things, and I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm dealing with anything like that. It's just the archiving instructions. Is that... does that sound like a better kind of experience to have, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do the voices seem to be triggered by any specific emotions or thoughts you're having at the time?

Oh, um... well, I don't think so? I really try to keep my thoughts very positive, you know. I wouldn't want to be sitting around dwelling on bad things and bringing this on myself. 

It really just seems to happen out of nowhere. Like I was saying, I'll just be in my apartment, minding my own business, or maybe I'm out at a museum, and I'll find myself in one of those quiet, empty rooms... and then the whispering just starts. It's those women behind the walls, very clearly telling me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I don't feel upset or stressed when it happens. I hope that's the right way to feel about it? I really don't think I'm doing anything to cause it, Doctor. I just want to be sure you don't think I'm bringing this on by having the wrong kinds of thoughts. Am I making sense?
Do you find that the voices are affecting your ability to work or take care of your daily responsibilities?

Oh, um... well, I really do try my very best to keep up with everything. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just letting things fall apart or being irresponsible. I've always prided myself on being very capable, you know?

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest—and I do want to be honest with you, Doctor—things have gotten a little... complicated lately. I... I've missed a few board meetings, and some bills might have slipped my mind. It's just so hard to focus on those things when the women are whispering about the archive. 

It's actually gotten to the point where... well, I hope you don't think less of me for this, but my cousin had to step in to help me with my money and appointments. And... and a museum administrator had to help out with some public events because I just couldn't manage them safely on my own anymore. I think I've even lost the trust of some of my colleagues, which just breaks my heart. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I really am trying to get back on track. Is it... is it understandable that I needed a little help? I just want to make sure I'm not failing at everything.
Do you believe the voices are actually coming from women who are trying to help you with the photographs, or do you think there might be some other explanation for what you're hearing?

Oh, well... I mean, I really do think they're real. The women, I mean. They sound so clear, just like you and I are talking right now. 

I know it probably sounds a little... unusual... to say there are women behind the walls or in the museum rooms. I hope you don't think I'm being silly or... or making things up. I really wouldn't do that. It's just that they're so helpful, telling me exactly which photographs belong in the archive. 

I suppose... well, I guess some people might say it's all in my head? But it just doesn't feel that way to me. They really do seem like they're trying to guide me. Is it... is it okay that I believe they're real, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way. I wouldn't want to be unreasonable about it.
Do you think the voices could be a product of your own mind, or do you believe they are definitely coming from outside of yourself?

Oh, um... well, I know you asked something similar just a moment ago, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or... or like I'm not listening to you. I promise I am listening carefully. 

It's just... to me, they definitely feel like they're coming from outside. Like I mentioned, it's those very clear voices I keep hearing when I'm in my apartment, or when I'm standing in one of those quiet, empty museum rooms. It really does sound exactly like women whispering from behind the walls, trying to tell me which photographs need to go into the archive. 

I know it might sound strange to say they're outside of me, but they just sound so real and distinct. I really hope I'm not being difficult by saying that. I just want to give you the most honest answer I can. Does that make sense? I hope it's alright that I'm experiencing it that way.
Do you think the information the voices give you about the photographs is always correct?

Oh, um... well, I really do try to follow their advice, because they seem so sure. I wouldn't want to ignore them if they're trying to be helpful. I always try to be a good listener, you know?

But... I suppose, if I really think about it... sometimes I do wonder. The voices, I mean. When I'm in my apartment, or standing in one of those empty museum rooms, and I hear the women whispering from behind the walls... they tell me exactly which photographs belong in the archive. And I want to believe they're right. 

But... well, I hope this doesn't make me sound ungrateful for their help, but sometimes the photographs they choose... they just don't seem to fit the collection. I try my best to make sense of it, but... maybe they aren't always completely correct? 

I'm sorry, I hope it's okay for me to question them like that. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for the archive. Do you think it's alright that I'm not entirely sure about the information they give me? I really want to be doing a good job with all of this.
Do you think the voices will always be there, or is it possible for them to go away completely?

Oh, um... I really hope they can go away. I mean, I want to do whatever you think is best, Doctor. If you think there's a way for them to stop... I would be so grateful. 

It's just... well, like I said, it's those clear voices I keep hearing in my apartment, and sometimes in those empty museum rooms. The women whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. It's... it's really the main reason I'm here talking to you today. That's what brought me in. 

I try to handle it as best as I can, and I hope I haven't been too much of a bother by talking about it so much. But it can be a little overwhelming, trying to listen to them and figure out the photographs all the time. Do you think... do you think there's a chance they might stop completely? I really want to be cooperative and do whatever treatment you suggest. I just want to feel a bit more normal, if that's okay to say?
Have you ever experienced anything like this before, with the voices or any other unusual perceptions?

Oh, um... well, before this started? No, I've never had anything quite like this happen before. I really hope I'm giving you the right information, I want to be as helpful as possible. 

It's just been this current... experience. I've been hearing the voices, and... well, I also have this absolute certainty that people are watching my archive. Both of those things have been present for about eight months now. 

I know eight months might sound like a long time to wait before getting help, and I'm so sorry if I should have come to see you sooner. I really tried to just manage it on my own at first, you know? I just didn't want to make a fuss or be a burden to anyone. I hope you're not disappointed in me for letting it go on for that long without saying anything. Do you think it's still alright that I'm here now? I really am ready to do whatever you think is best.
Do you think the women whispering from behind the walls could be mistaken about the photographs belonging in the archive?

Oh, um... well, I suppose it's possible they could be mistaken. I really don't want to sound like I'm criticizing them, though. I know they're probably just trying to help me. 

But... yes, I think they could be wrong sometimes. It's just... well, like I mentioned, the whole reason I'm here is because of these clear voices I keep hearing. When I'm in my apartment, or... or when I'm walking through those empty museum rooms, I hear these women whispering from right behind the walls. And they tell me exactly which photographs belong in the archive. 

I try to follow their instructions, I really do, because I want to do a good job. But sometimes I just... I look at the photographs they choose and I think, maybe they made a mistake? I hope it's okay that I'm questioning them like this. I don't want to seem ungrateful or difficult. Do you think it's normal for me to wonder if the voices might be wrong about the archive? I really just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Do you think it's possible that the voices are just a product of your own thoughts or imagination, rather than actually being women whispering from behind the walls?

Oh, um... well, I suppose... I mean, I know how it sounds. I really do. And I want to agree with you, Doctor, because I know you're the expert and you know best. I really hope I'm not being difficult by saying this...

But... it's just that they sound so real. Like I said, it's the main reason I came in to see you. When I'm in my apartment, or in those quiet, empty museum rooms... I hear them so clearly. It really sounds exactly like women whispering from right behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. 

I know it might seem like it's just my imagination, and I'm so sorry if I'm not explaining it right. I really wish I could just turn it off or tell myself it's not real. But when it happens, it doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all. It feels like they're really there. I hope that makes sense? I really want to give you the right answers so we can figure this out. Do you think... do you think it's still possible to treat it, even if it feels that real to me?
Do you think the people watching your archive are actually there, or could they be a product of your imagination?

Oh, um... well, I know it probably sounds like I'm letting my imagination run away with me. I really don't want to seem paranoid or—or like I'm making things up to be important. I hope you don't think I'm just being silly. 

But... I really am convinced they're actually there. The museum board, and the city arts people... I'm so sure they've been monitoring my phone. It's because they know my Caribbean archive is going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth about things. 

I'm sorry if that sounds a bit grand, I really don't mean to boast or anything. It's just... no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise, you know? It feels very real to me, even if it's hard for other people to understand. I really hope I'm not frustrating you by saying that. Do you... do you think it's okay that I feel so certain about it, even if you might think it's my imagination? I just want to be completely honest with you so I'm doing this right.
Do you think the importance of your archive and the voices' instructions about it are exaggerated or overly significant?

Oh, um... I really hope I don't sound like I have a swelled head or anything. I don't want you to think I'm arrogant or making a big fuss over nothing. I know a lot of people probably think their projects are more important than they really are...

But... well, I truly don't think I'm exaggerating. I mean, I'm just so convinced that the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone. And I know it's because my Caribbean archive is going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth about our history. 

I'm so sorry if that sounds a bit much. I really don't want to come across as difficult or full of myself. It's just that... well, no one has been able to show me anything that proves they aren't monitoring me, or that the archive isn't as important as I think it is. I hope it's okay that I still believe in it this strongly. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on... am I explaining this in a way that makes sense to you, Doctor?
Do you think other people share your belief about the significance of your Caribbean archive?

Oh, um... well... I hope you don't mind me bringing them up again. I know I just mentioned this, and I'm so sorry if I sound like a broken record... I really don't want to test your patience or take up too much of your time with the same things. 

But... yes, I do think some people realize how significant it is. I mean, the museum board and the city arts people must know. I'm still just so convinced that they've been monitoring my phone exactly *because* they know about it. They know my Caribbean archive is going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth. If they didn't think it was important, they wouldn't be keeping such close tabs on me, would they? 

And... well, no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise, so I just have to assume they see its value too, even if they're going about it in a frightening way. Does... does that make sense, Doctor? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for, I really just want to be as helpful as I can.
